evidence: Nestled along the western edge of Hanoi’s historic Old Quarter, Hang Da Street stands as a vibrant testament to the city’s rich tapestry of past and present. Historically, this thoroughfare was known as a hub for skilled leather workers, who crafted saddles and drumheads from buffalo and cow hides, giving rise to its original name, “Hang Da,” which translates to Leather Street.

The narrow alleyways, once lined with drying leather sheets, now host a thriving fashion district. Rows of closely packed tube houses, constructed with a blend of silver-gray glass and mossy-yellow concrete, create a visually striking landscape.
